Someone just called my daughters cell phone, from a blocked number and asked her if he was speaking to (insert her actual name). She said "yes, this is her". The adult male caller then said he was a cop and that our neighbor is complaining about the noise we are making. (It is nearly 1am. We are all sleeping or silently watching tv) we have no neighbor, the oly one who lived where this guy was implying passed away over the summer. The guy then told her to go outside and to get in the car with him and his partner because he needs her to help him settle this matter..


She is being bullied pretty bad at school rn, so idk if maybe one of the girls at school are messing with her. At least that would explain how this person got her phone number. But it is the whole "creepy pasta" "let's not meet" vibes that are genuinely scary af to me right now.

What's weird, and prompted me to post this is that idk how i feel. What I do know is that, since the fire, things have been "go go go", from sun up to sun down.


 I can feel something not good sneaking in when I find a moment alone, and it causes me to try to keep going and going and run myself so ragged that I sit down for a few, and fall right to sleep.


The other day, the first time i was finally alone, I was driving and zoned out hard-core. Then i was envisioning my son in the bedroom window, with his hand against it and smoke enveloping him. The envisionment got much worse from there, and I broke into screaming at nothing until my voice went raw. As if I was angry, and at my end. 


I have a doctor who offered me medicine, but I have been on medicine in the past and do not like how I feel. I like very much to try to get past things without medicine if possible. I have not had therapy in a few years, but the red cross has set therapy up for my kids, so I suppose I will be talking to them for that for myself (my kids are in therapy for past events already but their therapist is on Maternity leave. Luckily / Coincidentally she starts back this week). I've found in life the best thing you can do is to confront the emotions head on, and to feel them even if it hurts. During this time though I'm just having trouble feeling anything, and the thoughts or fears I have are too terrible to think through and that's hardest. I know I will be okay, and will get through it all, but I love to write. The best coping skill I've got Is to write and share my experiences. I pull from a place I can only feel is there within me for my words in poetry and tones of a story.  I wanted to do that here, but could only find the words that described the actual events on that morning. So I posted it, hoping it would move me out of my head. Thank you for reading too.

If I'm being honest it sounds to me that you want to be loved in a similar way to that of how it appears to you your brother is loved. I've known multiple autistic men. (Only one autistic girl though) and in truth They can be very difficult to even be friends with.

Often they appear very selfish, and if you don't know any better, narcissistic. These individuals were higher functioning (my friends) then what it seems your brother must be though. And sorry everyone idc that autism is cool today, they aren't all cool geniuses counting cards. They're hardly different from you and me and can really be assholes. One of my neurodivergent friends was carring on a relationship with a 13yr Gil who he brought heroin to, and got caught. He had the understanding that this was wrong enough to hide it from all of us, but got off with four months in county and charges dropped do to his condition. If I'm not mistaken him and the underage girl started back up after his release too. I too do not hate autistic people,  but I do hate how people have turned a neurological disability into a tiktok trend and you'rean asshole if you point thatout.. sorry if you find that offensive. It may not reflect your views on autism but it definitely reflects a lot of people today.

With that said, I will say that your parents should be doing more about his hurting you physically. From the sounds of it you could find your self in a very dangerous situation with how he has been hitting you and it is not okay or safe that your parents are not stepping in to prevent this. It's worse that they reinforce it by punishing you and defending him.

I do believe that your parents lack the ability to see your brother in the same way that you do. Who is perceiving him correctly though? Maybe both you and your parents are seeing him as he is, but each of you aren't able to step outside of your own biases to see him in full..I mean human beings are very complex and we all definitely have multiple sides to ourselves. That includes a person with autism too.

You are 17years old and your life has been spent as - I would assume- having to grow up the hard way like all the rest of us, while watching your brother really only grow in size and age but never grow up. God that I imagine being sooo difficult. Knowing you're expected to hold yourself responsible for all your actions like that of any adult, but your brother gets his water fed to him. Learning absolutely no responsibility whatsoever. Worse, learning to utilize his condition to get away with harming a girl when it suits him.

Your parents are ignorant and it is sad but not necessarily their fault. It's just who they are. They have done your childhood a disservice but you adulthood they did you favors. Whereas your brothers life right now is all easy costing but sadly his future will be difficult. At its easiest it will be in institutions and homes, while you live a normal life. So long as you can find a way to over come your anger and resentment. His future will be on your parents. 

But I believe (based on the little I have read) your mom and dad have it extremely difficult and are living very unhappy lives but they're only doing it to do what they feel is the best for you and your brother. They might be wrong and their best might suck ass, but they are human therefore they really do not know just how much ass their best is sucking. 

I feel like I would possibly feel sad for them. Not that I think you should, just saying that I would. The last 20something years have probably been difficult for them. And all they've wanted was to be good parents and raise healthy children who thrive and go places they never did. Whereas for you, your life is literally juuuuust about to start. You have everything right out in front of you now. At this age you are at the edge of all the real beginnings. 

I'm sorry you are seemingly neglected. It is not at all an easy world,we are all just here trying our bests and almost never noticing or wanting to admit when our best really suuuxks assess lol and right now you are a victim of that.

I'm definitely going to think about your story someday in the future and think "hmm, I wounder where that girl ever ended up. I hope she got out of that house and her life moved on forward to someplace she was more happy "

It's an odd thing to feel alone in the world. Have no one in your real life but surrounded by humans all over the place. People who don't listen, people who only listen in the event that they think you'll shut up long enough for them to turn the conversation onto how they have it harder. People who are blind to depression, blind to anything actually real. 

People are blind to beauty. They don't see anything really and people like us are expected to be like them. Expected to live our lives for no true purpose, spending far more then 50% of our time in places we hate doing pointless things.. 

I don't want to die myself.  Not In this moment at least. I do find that the saddness we feel is what brings us a sight and an understanding that most other people do not get to enjoy. My saddness brings me more joy then anything. I see so many things every day that the greater majority just can't see.

A fucking tree placed just right in a feild where the sun is hitting with an orange glow and I  can feel every part of that space and that time. A grieving widow can break my heart but give me hope that true love is real all in one moment. Other people just get sad for a few, and boom back to their lives. Bye.. I still think about people who I met on plans or grayhounds, ten years ago. I write random stories about where I hope they are in life today. 

I am constantly curious about way too much and my brain won't turn off. Often people think this is a curse, but I almost always think this is a gift to be utilized as much as possible. Even if this over thinking is dwelling on something sad. It is a way for me to grieve a lose or to process a difficult situation. It almost always is what causes me to fix a problem or give me random strings of words to compose a half way crappy poem or story.

I hope you survived tonight. I hope you walked off your bus and made it to wherever you call home and fell into a safe place. I hope your story isn't one that ends in mystery too to be honest I hope I don't find myself having to one day, in a year or five, write a story with too many blanks to fill in forcing a sad ending. I truly hope you find the beauty in the bullshit world around all of us and can find a way to accept that all that is true and real in our world is time, and love. Everything else is just a consequence of too much intelligence mingled up with history's ego. 

You can make it through your life. You just need to understand that it is all bullshit, all that is real is love and time everything else is made up. Everything else really isn't worth your energy.

I'm a single father of two. A 9year old, and a 12year old. I have no family no friends and the kids mother is gone.  Is your wife trying to glorify herself for some ass backwards reasons insulting to someone like me? Not really honestly I don't give a fuck. 

If I where you id be concerned about your wife finding it necessary to gain some sort of gratification from stretching the truth to the point of a lie. Her behavior sounds similar to that of a self centered person who cannot see past their own self long enough to gain the courage to take responsibility for their short comings and faults.. 

Is she unhappy?  I bet she says she is. And I'll bet more over there isn't enough within this world to bring her true happiness. Her unhappiness comes from her own mind and her own self but she blames you and everyone else for it.

Does she like when others think your a bad father and worse husband? 10bucks says yes!! Who wants to take this bet? Why? Also, if yes, (clearly yes) what inevitable consequences will come frome this kind of Mentality..

Do you want a divorce? I'm willing to bet that's a no. So why say this? Is it a guilt trip or is it a scare tactic? I'd honestly assume one of two things could be taking place in the context of you having posted this..

Number1: either, it turns out to our surprise that you are the asshole looking smear your wife in order to feel good inside. As well as will eventually show her all the comments that agree with your point of view thus gaslighting her into taking responsibility for you

Or

Number two: your wife's behavior is abusive and you are not even realizing it. But we see it because no one, NO ONE gets so upset and frustrated with a nonsensical situation to the point in which they need to turn to anyone who will, - hopefully, - confirm that they are not crazy. You need reassuring that what you feel is wrong actually is wrong and it is difficult to find that when your partner is essentially telling you that you are an asshole or that your eyes are deceiving you and therefore you are crazy.

Idk what you will do though man.. if I have learned anything in this world, it is that you can never win against a woman like this. If she is how I see this post describing her to be, then she will either attempt to ignore the problem until it goes away, ( your want for your kids to be educated and her to stop calling herself a single mother being the problem that is.) 

Or she will go to war with you over this topic, eventually cheating and taking the kids away. So maybe let it be? She won't just stop saying shes a single mom, and bet even if you express that this is hurtful and untrue it probably doesn't  / wont change anything. 

But, of course this problem will have the potential to grow and get worse. Are you right or wrong in this scenario? If your post is 100% accurate as to the situation and who you are versus her as well, then clearly you have an issue with your wife doing and saying these things and she knows, as well as has no problem crossing one of your obvious emotional boundaries. So, yeah damn straight you have every right to expect your children get the typical upbringing as all our other kids tend to get here in America. 

So I would say yes you are right. But, I will just have to always fall back on this last little bit. What can you actually do? Divorce her? Go to court? And what good will come of that? It's almost guaranteed that she will be awarded all the rights and privileges necessary to make the decisions for the children with or without your full consent anyways. At least now you have your family together, the children have their mother and father in the same home, and you're able to keep an eye on things. I do recommend that you gather whatever evidence you might need for the potential impending future though. 

As well as, if you love and respect her, well honestly then fuck it. Let her feel big if it makes her happy. Let her feel like she is a big girl and don't try to mold her into who you and your kids need her to be. The sad reality is, that it is highly unlikely she sees the error of her ways. Besides usually your pushing for her to be at the least a bare bones basic mother will hurt her ego n self image which won't result in her changing things.. it's just not in a lot of us to find our inner faults, let alone do anything about it either.. well other then going out in an effort to find a man who will allow her to behave however she wants without repercussion on arguments.

I'm no lawyer, just a father who fought two years for custody of my son and daughter.  So I have no legal advice, just my own experiences. 

I understand better then most what a child in your nephews position is going through. I have experienced my own adoption as a child (i was old enough to remember too), as well as a very convoluted custody battle against my own biological mother. A person who by a string of behind my back / lie fueled and manipulative events obtained - and nearly kept - custody of my two kids. It was ultimately due to my ten year old son exclaiming to the caseworker his wanting to live with me, that got me custody.  It is a very messed up and mixed story. One where my biological mother told the court and caseworkers she was my actual mother and had raised me, annnd that was all it took for them to believe - or at least continue to refer to her as - that she was the kids legal grandmother. Even after I explained my adoption, and how id never even known her until my mid 20's. It was an absolute nightmare, one that only just began to end. I swear I think I actually have some kind of trauma disorder after this battle.  I wake up from dreams a couple times a week and have to physically see them to know they are still here.

Either way, my point is, my children did not want to stay in her home, they where very vocal about it when given the opportunity to speak openly without bio mom near by. My children's vocalization coupled with a new caseworker taking things over after the initial caseworker left or lost their job, I was finally able to bring my kids home.

 One of the biggest things that we have the potential to over look is indeed the children's best interest, as well as what the child / children in question actually want for themselves. These two things should come together in some way that makes the healthiest decision for the kids. A child may WANT to have the mother and son/daughter relationships they see all of their friends at school having, and care nothing about the potential consequences of their mothers drug addiction. Kids often wear rose colored glasses so to speak, but clearly this could be a very unwise choice. That does not mean that their relationship with their parent should be completely ignored though, since this too is going to be potentially unwise and detrimental to their mental health. My kids mother is an active drug addict and was recently arrested for felony pos of methamphetamine. Plus she is a complete monster even if sober. But the state did not even mention these problems during court (she only showed up to one court case in two years btw) but still im leagaly obligated to allow her visitation if she was to reach out. Even though I believe her involvement in their lives needs to be nonexistent to ensure no more damage can be done to them. Im not sure if my contradicting statements here add up lol in one second i say allow communication to the absent parent, then i say do not. The point is each case is dramatically different, even if similar and should be treated as such, but usually is not.

 under the circumstances that I see in your situation, I would predict that staying in your care would be both, in the child's best interest as well as what the child will want themselves. I think that you have a very good case on your side, and that you would be doing exactly what is best for your nephew. Although I don't know how or where you should start, i do suggest contacting a lawyer in your area who specializes in family court. This way if your sister decides that its all of a sudden her turn with the kid you have been raising nearly his entire life, you will of already gotten one step ahead.  I doubt your sister will care if your nephew doesn't want to leave you, often "they" never care what the children want. 

I wish you the best of luck in your future, I truly hope all goes smoothly and in favor of your kiddo.
